claims.text: The clauses distinguish relinquishment from cession, including US occupation obligations for Cuba. Signature differs from effect: ratifications were exchanged in April 1899. Spain and the United States’ records establish neither residents’ consent, unrestricted self-government nor either place’s whole history. Puerto Rico’s statute prescribes US appointment with Senate consent; Cuba’s French edition, Spanish original uncollated, prescribes indirect presidential election. MJP’s modern introduction describes intervention constraints. Wood reports a 1902 transfer to Cuba’s President and Congress. Prescriptions and reports establish neither unrestricted sovereignty nor operation.
